newsitem.title: USA: New Hampshire police seeking kilts.
newsitem.headline: New Hampshire police seeking kilts.

text.p: Police in this small town in the White Mountains of New Hampshire are trying to raise money to buy kilts to wear during a three-day Scottish festival.
Lincoln Police Sgt. Michael Tamulonis said the town of 1,300 people annually hosts some 35,000 people for the festival and the police want to add to the colour at the event.

"I've had the idea to wear a kilt for a long time, but the cost is prohibitive," Tamulonis said. At $300-to-$500 per kilt, the police department could ill afford to buy the kilts for its eight full-time and five part-time officers.
So Tamulonis, who is of Lithuanian descent, and the other officers have launched a "Kilts for Cops" fundraising campaign.

The local Citizens Bank, a subsidiary of the Royal Bank of Scotland, has opened up an account for the kilts and Tamulonis reports he has received several donations including a "$15 check from a woman we helped when she was locked out of her car last summer.
"A local man has donated the socks and a supplier has said he will sell us the hats at wholesale," Tamulonis said.
The kilts themselves will not hinder the officers in performing their duties.
"The kilts have a belt and that's where we'll wear our duty belt" upon which they will have their guns, handcuffs, nightsticks and mace, he said. "We'll still be police. We'll just be in kilts."
"We'll use the New Hampshire state tartan. It's blue with streaks of purple in it. It's really beautiful," Tamulonis said.
